name: InterContinental Buckhead Atlanta
positioning: City hotel in Atlanta's Buckhead neighborhood, an easy half-mile walk from Lenox Square, with a 21st-floor Club InterContinental lounge, a spa beside a heated saltwater pool, and The Americano restaurant helmed by chef Scott Conant
best_for: Shoppers who want to walk to Lenox Square and Shops Around Lenox
Travelers who want a club lounge, spa and heated outdoor pool under one roof in Buckhead

facts.text: The hotel is in Atlanta's Buckhead neighborhood.
The hotel is one block from MARTA and provides access to Buckhead Village and Lenox Square.
The rotunda lobby has high-backed chairs around small tables, marble floors and giant planters.
Works by Atlanta-based mixed media artist Niki Zarrabi adorn the walls of the Great Hall.
Rooms and suites have designer furniture and monogrammed motifs inspired by Atlanta's architecture.
Rooms have a luxurious soaking tub.
Rooms have pillow-top beds and a separate shower and tub.
The spa is paired with an adjacent fitness center and a heated outdoor saltwater pool.
Spa treatments range from antioxidant facials to lavender mud wraps.
The fitness center has Peloton bikes.
Cabanas can be booked at Peachtree Pool, with a cheese and charcuterie board paired with Chandon Garden Spritz or Whispering Angel Rosé.
The Americano is helmed by chef Scott Conant and features fine steaks, freshly made pasta, Mediterranean seafood and an extensive wine list.

highlights.text: Twin murals by Atlanta-based mixed media artist Niki Zarrabi in the Great Hall feature Georgia's state flower, the Cherokee Rose.
The Club InterContinental lounge is a fully staffed 21st-floor lounge with daily complimentary breakfast, snacks and evening refreshments.
The heated saltwater Peachtree Pool and Sun Terrace are open year-round.
The Presidential Suites feature original artwork, plush furnishings and a dual-sided fireplace.
It is an easy half-mile walk along Peachtree Road to Lenox Square and Shops Around Lenox.

considerations.text: A daily destination fee is applied to each room.
WhataHotel notes that the urban setting may lack a resort-style atmosphere.
